sentences.text: "Duke" Austin, Jr. has served as a board member, president and chief executive officer of Quanta Services since March 2016, after holding the role of chief operating officer from January 2013 until January 2022.

Earlier at Quanta he was president of the Electric Power Division and Oil and Gas Division from May 2011 to December 2012, president of the Oil and Gas Division from October 2009 to May 2011, and president of North Houston Pole Line, L.P., an electric and natural gas specialty contractor and Quanta subsidiary, from 2001 until September 2009.

sentences.text: He holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in business management from Sam Houston State University.
He also chairs the Texas State University System Board of Regents and is a director of the Southwest Line Chapter of the National Electrical Contractors Association.

sentences.text: "Duke" Austin Jr. has led Quanta Services as president and CEO since March 2016, joining through the acquisition of North Houston Pole Line and previously serving as chief operating officer and division president, and he also sits on the board.

sentences.quote: Quanta reported revenue of $28.5 billion (+20% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of $2.9 billion, adjusted EPS of $10.75, free cash flow of $1.7 billion, and ended the year with a record backlog of $44 billion.
sentences.text: Under him, 2025 revenue reached a record $28.5 billion, up 20 percent, with $1.7 billion of free cash flow, record year-end backlog of $44 billion, eight acquisitions completed and leverage held below 2x.
Capital deployment also includes buybacks, such as roughly $135 million of stock in the first quarter of 2025.
Backlog reached an all-time high of $53.44 billion in the second quarter of 2026.

sentences.text: Record total backlog of $53.4 billion at June 30, 2026, up from $35.8 billion a year earlier, gives Quanta Services multi-year revenue visibility.
Quanta's Electric Infrastructure Solutions segment produced second-quarter 2026 revenues of $7.8 billion at an 11.5% operating margin, up from 10.1% a year earlier.
Management points to the convergence of utility, power generation and large-load demand as a source of significant opportunity.
